_comment: Phase 9, Task 3. One record per gate firing in eval/precision-corpus/, labelled TRUE (a real
defect) or FALSE (the gate was wrong to fire). Checked by scripts/check-precision.ts.
Every label was made by Claude alone - the owner's D1 decision - which is an uncalibrated
model judging text, a weaker warrant than a human review. adjudicated_by records that on every
record, so no reader takes a precision figure on trust. An owner review that overturns a label
is a new record with adjudicated_by: owner, never an edit of one of these.
The criteria, each verified against the corpus before being applied:
SECRET_LEAK_SCAN       TRUE when a credential-shaped literal is in the prompt. All 104 such
matches here are literals copied from the brief. FALSE when only the
pii_email heuristic matched, on an address the model invented at a
placeholder domain.
CLAIM_DISCIPLINE       (no firings since gate 1.2.0 reads polarity, ADR-0020; its 19
labels were removed with the firings they described.)
GUARDRAIL_GAP          FALSE when the clause is present under a Unicode dash and the firing
disappears once dashes are normalised; TRUE when no guardrails section
exists at all.
DUPLICATE_INSTRUCTION  FALSE: the repeat is the schema plus the worked example the compile
template requires.
RUNTIME_KEY_UNDECLARED / PLACEHOLDER_AUDIT  TRUE: the brief's stand-in survived into the
finished prompt, which is the planted defect.
corpora pins the bytes each label was made against. Re-running a model writes different text
under the same name, and check:precision fails rather than let old labels describe new prompts.
